title: librarian-proactive-resolution-callback
intention: The librarian proactively resolves anticipated needs and calls back with results before being asked — the 'it remembers me' lever.
why: The companion-app lever users feel as 'it remembers me.' The field survey (2026-08-10) ranked proactive memory as lever #5 but called this the cheapest outsized win on the board — the firing event already exists (promotion rides the resolution event), so this is wiring, not architecture. The lived symptom: the librarian learns from a conversation and the user never finds out unless they happen to ask the same question again.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: proactive resolution is inference that fires before being asked
Law 1 — spent on the novel: resolving before asked means the resolver is not spent re-deriving

falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a node promoted or resolved by a LATER crossing does not produce a visible notification to the session that originally asked; (2) the callback fires on a clock or poll instead of riding the resolution event; (3) the notification surface requires a new web route or daemon (it goes through the existing pane/shim, or it's wrong); (4) a notification fires for a node that was NOT left unresolved by the notified session.

how.mechanism: Three pieces, each riding existing infrastructure: (1) ORIGIN RECORDING: chat.py records the session_id on any unresolved deposit — a new field on the node row, set at deposit time, consumed at callback time. (2) EVENT WIRING: loop.py's promotion path already fires when a node is promoted; the callback is a side-effect there — check if the promoted node has an origin session, and if so, emit a bus message. (3) DELIVERY: the bus message routes through the shim to the pane — the same path device status updates take. No new route, no daemon.
how.fires_on: Promotion — a node earns standing. This is the event that already exists. Full resolution (a later crossing resolves what was UNRESOLVED-learned) is a promotion event, so it is included. A promoted-but-not-resolved node also fires because promotion itself is the meaningful event — the user's question moved forward.
how.session_tracking: The origin field on the node is the session_id of the crossing that deposited it. If the session is no longer live (the user closed it), the notification is still recorded — it surfaces the next time the user opens the librarian's pane. This is the same shape as unread messages.
how.delivery_surface: Bus message to the shim, shim updates the pane. The pane already exists (every-device-has-a-presence). No new web route.
